# pytest-databricks-lakeflow

> A pytest plugin for testing the Lakeflow Jobs in a Databricks Asset Bundle. A test points at a job or a task in the bundle, the plugin deploys the bundle once per session, creates a throwaway copy of the job for the test, runs it with the chosen parameters, returns the per-task state, outputs, logs, printed notebook output, errors, task values and resolved parameters, and deletes the job. Task-level tests wrap one task with injected tasks that set upstream task values and capture the values it sets.

Install with `uv add --dev "pytest-databricks-lakeflow[connect]"` or `pip install "pytest-databricks-lakeflow[connect]"`; the `connect` extra installs databricks-connect, which runs setup=, teardown= and once() steps over Databricks Connect in seconds, and installs only on Python 3.12, so elsewhere the steps run as 30 second tasks. Requires Python 3.11 or later, the Databricks CLI v1.7.0 or later, and credentials for a workspace with serverless jobs. The public API is importable from `pytest_databricks_lakeflow`: `Lakeflow`, `EphemeralJob`, `EphemeralPipeline`, `RunHandle`, `JobRun`, `TaskRun`, `TaskValues`, `TaskError`, `StepResult`, `Timing`, `NotebookView`, `NotebookCell`, `SqlResult`, `PipelineUpdate`, `DebugNotebook`, `ForEachStats`, `ForEachError`, `DbtArtifacts`, `DbtResult`, `Stub`, `SweepReport`, `ALL_RULES`, `DEFAULT_RULES`, `LakeflowError`, `LakeflowBundleError`, `LakeflowTimeout`, `LakeflowRunFailed`. Tests get a `Lakeflow` from the session-scoped `lakeflow` fixture.

## Documentation

- [Home](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/): the README, with the pitch, a job test, a task test and the fixture override
- [Getting started](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/getting-started/): prerequisites, install, the bundle test target, reading catalog and schema from job parameters, configuring the fixture, the first test, running it
- [Job tests](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/job-tests/): lakeflow.job() and its options, run() and its options, checking the outcome (succeeded, task(), raise_for_failure(), repr), the TaskRun fields, asserting on a failure (raised(), error.root_cause, error.code, output_json), reading task values with capture_task_values, temporary schemas with lakeflow.schema(), run(only=...) and what it refuses, what happens when a test fails
- [Task tests](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/task-tests/): lakeflow.task() and its options, how stubs resolve, rules for stub values, Stub(values=..., outputs=...) for output references, reading captured values, upstream_from to replay a task from a previous run, testing a condition task alone, running a for-each body once with input=, helper compute, what a single-task job loses
- [Recipes](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/recipes/): an "I want to..." index of every recipe
  - [Change the job settings](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/recipes/job-settings/): disable, task_params, task_overrides (retries and timeouts), run_as, extra_dependencies and local wheels with extras, environments=, modify_settings, Lakeflow defaults and dataclasses.replace
  - [Control the run](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/recipes/runs/): upstream_task_values on job() with only, replay=, start() and RunHandle, stop_after, max_concurrent_runs, shared runs in a fixture, parametrize and xdist
  - [Task types](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/recipes/task-types/): SQL file rows (sql_result), saved_queries="inline", alert_state, branches and force_conditions, for_each_inputs and iterations, trigger=, pipeline refresh options, pipeline_update, pipelines="copy", lakeflow.pipeline(), Run Job tasks (children, child_run), dbt tasks (task_params, dbt_commands, dbt_artifacts), other task outputs
  - [Test data](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/recipes/data/): lakeflow.schema(), lakeflow.once() for fixtures every test reads (once per session, across xdist workers, torn down at session end), setup= and teardown= steps over Databricks Connect by default, teardown_at="close", SQL statement lists and .py notebook files, run_as_task=True to run steps as tasks, StepResult, seeding with pytester, test_marker
  - [Debug a failure](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/recipes/debugging/): failure messages, --lakeflow-live and stream=, TaskRun.notebook and notebook_export, keep rules and --lakeflow-keep-ttl, lakeflow.attach(run_id), debug_notebook() and --lakeflow-debug-notebook, --lakeflow-report-dir
  - [Compute and cost](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/recipes/compute/): performance_target (PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZED by default, STANDARD for cheap CI, the --lakeflow-performance-target flag) and run(performance_target=...), queue, existing_cluster_id, single_node, helpers_compute, environment_version and helpers_environment_version, budget_policy_id, where setup and teardown steps run over Databricks Connect and what they cost, modify_settings compute recipes, run_finished timings to CSV
  - [Bundle deployments](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/recipes/deployments/): target and variables, the host check, sync strategies and strict_artifacts, per-branch and per-identity deployments, deploy_flags, --lakeflow-destroy
  - [CI and housekeeping](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/recipes/ci/): a CI pipeline with a service principal, children="refuse" and keep_failed=False, permissions, lakeflow.check() with rules= and --lakeflow-check, the --lakeflow-sweep flags, Lakeflow.sweep() from a script
- Reference
  - [Lakeflow arguments](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/reference/lakeflow/): every Lakeflow argument with its default, defaults for per-call arguments, properties
  - [Command-line flags and environment variables](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/reference/flags/): every --lakeflow-* flag, the environment variables, what the sweep deletes
  - [Logs and reports](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/reference/output/): log lines, live output, JUnit XML properties, the lakeflow report section, the terminal summary, the report directory and report.json
  - [API](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/reference/api/): generated from the docstrings, and the ValueError versus LakeflowError rule
  - [Limitations](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/reference/limitations/): what the plugin cannot do, or does differently from the platform, and why
- [FAQ](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/faq/): the questions and error messages that come up most
- [How it works](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/how-it-works/): session setup, session steps (once()), parallel sessions, how a copy is built, created, run and torn down, pipeline copies, session end, what stays in the workspace, timing
- [Speed and cost](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/speed/): where a session's time goes (the deploy, the per-copy overhead, the 30 second serverless task floor, setup and teardown steps over Databricks Connect in seconds), the three rules (fixtures once, one worker per test, lakeflow.ws), sizing -n against the Jobs API limits, performance modes and DBUs, measuring with timing and the billing system tables
- [Changelog](https://stevenayers.github.io/pytest-databricks-lakeflow/changelog/)
